supporting_observations.claim: The reported time and the recorded PowerShell activity do not align exactly: at about 13:40, the records show a Windows logon and normal user-session startup, while the suspicious PowerShell process appears at 13:44:46.
At 13:44, Maria opened Downloads\Statement.docm in Word; Word then spawned PowerShell with no profile, a hidden window, and an encoded command.

The encoded PowerShell command decodes to an expression that downloads and executes a script from raw.githubusercontent.com/harbor-dental-it/tools/main/u.ps1; the proxy recorded a successful GET for that same URL.
PowerShell then launched rundll32 to invoke Init from C:\Users\maria.lopez\AppData\Roaming\svchelper.dll.
The Word-to-hidden-PowerShell-to-downloaded-script-to-rundll32 sequence is strongly indicative of malicious execution, rather than routine approved workstation patching.

known_telemetry_limitations: The supplied process records show the rundll32 command line but do not establish whether svchelper.dll was successfully loaded or what its contents were. (T023-00096, T023-00097)
The proxy records establish a successful request for u.ps1 but do not provide the script's contents in the supplied evidence. (T023-00089)
The supplied records do not show PowerShell starting at the reported 13:40 time; they show the suspicious PowerShell process at 13:44:46. (T023-00055, T023-00057, T023-00085)
claims_not_established: Whether Statement.docm was intentionally opened by Maria or how it was delivered.
The contents, provenance, and authorization status of u.ps1 and svchelper.dll.
Whether svchelper.dll executed successfully, established persistence, or performed further actions.
Whether credentials, data, or other sensitive information were accessed or exfiltrated.
additional_evidence_needed: Isolate WS-MLOPEZ-01 and preserve its volatile state and forensic image.
Collect Statement.docm, u.ps1, svchelper.dll, and relevant temporary files; calculate hashes and analyze their contents.
Collect endpoint protection and detailed file, image-load, and persistence telemetry for the host around and after 13:44 UTC.
Review the proxy response body or other retained copy of u.ps1, and verify the repository's ownership and history.
Review subsequent activity from the host for credential use, lateral movement, persistence, and data access or transfer.
